attachments.landmark_a: basilar part and the margin of the foramen magnum

bands.name: Transverse ligament of the atlas

attachments.landmark_b: opposite lateral mass of the atlas, passing behind the dens

bands.mechanical_role: primary restraint to anterior translation of the atlas on the axis
bands.function_note: The single most important stabiliser of the atlanto-axial joint: it holds the dens against the anterior arch of the atlas and keeps it out of the spinal canal. Rupture, or erosion by rheumatoid pannus, allows atlanto-axial subluxation and cord compression. Its laxity in Down syndrome is why screening precedes contact sport.
bands.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed.; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

bands.name: Cruciate ligament (transverse + longitudinal bands)

attachments.landmark_b: body of the axis (inferior longitudinal band)

bands.mechanical_role: cross-shaped reinforcement built around the transverse ligament
bands.function_note: The transverse ligament plus its vertical bands. The vertical bands contribute little mechanically; the transverse part does the work.
bands.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed.; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

bands.name: Alar ligaments

attachments.landmark_a: sides of the apex of the dens
attachments.landmark_b: medial aspect of each occipital condyle

bands.mechanical_role: primary restraint to contralateral axial rotation and to lateral bending
bands.function_note: Paired and obliquely set, so each limits rotation to the OPPOSITE side. They are the reason atlanto-axial rotation stops near 45 degrees, and their asymmetric tension is the basis of the alar ligament stress test.
bands.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed.; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

bands.name: Apical ligament of the dens

attachments.landmark_b: anterior margin of the foramen magnum

bands.function_note: Mechanically insignificant -- an embryological remnant of the notochord rather than a real restraint.
bands.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed.; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

bands.name: Tectorial membrane

attachments.landmark_a: body of the axis, continuing the posterior longitudinal ligament
attachments.landmark_b: basilar part, inside the foramen magnum

bands.mechanical_role: limits extension and forward translation at the craniovertebral junction
bands.function_note: The upward continuation of the posterior longitudinal ligament, forming the anterior wall of the vertebral canal at this level and separating the ligaments in front from the dura behind.
bands.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed.; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

bands.name: Anterior and posterior atlanto-occipital membranes

attachments.landmark_a: anterior and posterior arches of the atlas
attachments.landmark_b: anterior and posterior margins of the foramen magnum

bands.mechanical_role: close the gaps between the skull and the atlas
bands.function_note: The posterior membrane is pierced by the vertebral artery and the suboccipital nerve; it is sometimes ossified into a posterior ponticle (arcuate foramen), a variant relevant to cervical instrumentation.
bands.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed.; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

bands.name: Anterior and posterior atlantoaxial membranes

attachments.landmark_a: anterior and posterior arches of the atlas
attachments.landmark_b: body and lamina of the axis

bands.mechanical_role: close the gaps between the atlas and axis, supplementing the cruciate/alar/apical ligament complex
bands.function_note: The anterior atlantoaxial membrane is a broad band reinforced centrally by a strong fibrous cord continuous with the anterior longitudinal ligament; the posterior atlantoaxial membrane is thinner, comparable to a ligamentum flavum at this level, and is pierced by the C2 (greater occipital) nerve as it passes to the posterior neck.
bands.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

bands.name: Lateral atlanto-occipital ligament
bands.mechanical_role: limits excessive contralateral lateral flexion (side-bending) at the atlanto-occipital joint
bands.function_note: A short, quadrilateral thickening at the lateral margin of the atlanto-occipital joint capsule, distinct from the anterior/posterior atlanto-occipital membranes that close the gaps in the midline.
bands.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

function: Stabilise the atlanto-occipital and atlanto-axial joints, which have shallow articular surfaces and depend almost entirely on ligaments rather than bony congruity. Their integrity is what keeps the dens out of the spinal cord, so this is the one ligament complex whose failure is immediately life-threatening.
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed.; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)
